before: Avalanche (AVAX) is a layer-1 blockchain platform known for its speed and low transaction costs. It uses a unique consensus mechanism and supports multiple virtual machines for flexibility.
after: Avalanche (AVAX) is a blockchain network supporting smart contracts. Compare the relevant network documentation and observations rather than assuming fixed fees or confirmation times.

before: Litecoin (LTC) is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created as a 'lighter' version of Bitcoin. It offers faster transaction confirmations (2.5 min blocks) and uses the Scrypt hashing algorithm.
after: Litecoin (LTC) is a proof-of-work cryptocurrency using the Scrypt hashing algorithm. Block targets are protocol parameters; actual confirmation times and transaction costs depend on network conditions.

before: Intel Corporation is a semiconductor giant known for PC processors. It's undergoing a major transformation to compete in AI and regain manufacturing leadership with its foundry services.
after: Intel (INTC) designs semiconductors and operates chip-manufacturing businesses. Use company reports to separate current results from stated foundry plans; a turnaround hypothesis is not a price forecast.

before: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF is a low-cost alternative to SPY, tracking the same S&P 500 index. Popular for long-term investors due to its minimal expense ratio.
after: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) seeks to track the S&P 500 Index. Compare dated fund disclosures for objectives, holdings and costs rather than assuming a permanent cost advantage.

before: The US Dollar against the Japanese Yen—a key carry trade indicator and risk sentiment gauge. USD/JPY reflects interest rate differentials between the Fed and Bank of Japan.
after: USD/JPY quotes Japanese yen per US dollar. Changes can be compared with stated interest-rate assumptions, but the pair alone does not identify carry positions or establish market-wide risk sentiment.
